## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## claude.ai Linear
When passing string values to tools, send the content directly without escape sequences. For example, use real newlines in markdown content rather than literal backslash-n (\n) characters.

## penpot
You have access to Penpot tools in order to interact with Penpot designs.
Before working with these tools, be sure to read the 'Penpot High-Level Overview' via the `high_level_overview` tool.

## plugin:context7:context7
Use this server to fetch current documentation whenever the user asks about a library, framework, SDK, API, CLI tool, or cloud service — even well-known ones like React, Next.js, Prisma, Express, Tailwind, Django, or Spring Boot. This includes API syntax, configuration, version migration, library-specific debugging, setup instructions, and CLI tool usage. Use even when you think you know the answer — your training data may not reflect recent changes. Prefer this over web search for library docs.

Do not use for: refactoring, writing scripts from scratch, debugging business logic, code review, or general programming concepts.

## plugin:microsoft-docs:microsoft-learn
# Microsoft Learn MCP Server

This server gives structured access to official Microsoft and Azure documentation via three tools:

## Tools

### microsoft_docs_search
Search official documentation and return up to 10 concise, high-quality content chunks (max 500 tokens each), including title, URL, and excerpt.

- Use first to get a quick, reliable overview
- Ideal for grounding answers in Microsoft knowledge

### microsoft_code_sample_search
Search for code snippets and examples in official Microsoft Learn documentation and return up to 20 relevant, high-quality code samples.

- Use when you need to provide sample Microsoft/Azure related code in your answers.  
- Ideal for generating code snippets or practical implementation examples.  
- Optional parameter `language` can filter results. 

### microsoft_docs_fetch
Fetch and convert full Microsoft documentation pages to markdown.

- Use after search when you need full content from a specific URL
- Required for detailed tutorials, troubleshooting, prerequisites, code samples, or when search results are incomplete or outdated

## Workflow

1. Use `microsoft_docs_search` to find relevant documents.
2. If you need code examples or practical snippets, use `microsoft_code_sample_search`.
3. If deeper or complete information is needed, use `microsoft_docs_fetch`.

**Search gives breadth. Code Sample Search gives practical examples. Fetch gives depth.**

All content comes from Microsoft Learn or official sources, returned in clean markdown format.

{"id":"SMA-573","title":"ci: pin that repo:affected-smoke still declares the inputs every ci_targets pin depends on","description":"Follow-up from <issue id="0ef07e2a-4b63-45ab-892c-d3187bc4ad3d" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-530/ci-run-the-negative-control-self-test-of-release-parity-in-ci">SMA-530</issue>, recorded there as limitation **L1** in `ci/release-parity/README.md`.

## Gap

Every pin in `ci/affected-graph/ci_targets.py` — `RUN_SH_CALL_SITES`, `SELF_SCHEDULED_GATES`, `ACTIONLINT_SH_CALL_SITES`, `RELEASE_PARITY_SH_CALL_SITES` — only fires when `repo:affected-smoke` is scheduled. That gate's `inputs` list in `moon.yml` is what makes each of them reachable, and **nothing pins that list.**

Deleting an entry is silent, and worse, self-concealing:

* Removing `- 'moon.yml'` is itself a root-`moon.yml` edit. Afterwards the task's remaining globs do **not** match the root file — `*/moon.yml` matches `rs/moon.yml`, not `moon.yml`; `.moon/**/*` does not match it either — so the removal PR does not schedule the gate, and every later PR can delete a pinned line with nothing red.
* Removing `- 'ci/release-parity/**/*'` (added by <issue id="0ef07e2a-4b63-45ab-892c-d3187bc4ad3d" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-530/ci-run-the-negative-control-self-test-of-release-parity-in-ci">SMA-530</issue>) or `- 'ci/actionlint/**/*'` (added by <issue id="df30b176-c28c-4213-bfef-bff2f13c08cc" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-542/repo-actionlint-gate-guard-the-self-test-invocations-from-deletion">SMA-542</issue>) silently un-reaches that haystack's pin for every subsequent PR. Both entries carry "do not remove" comments, which is currently the **only** enforcement.

`repo:input-liveness` does not close this: it asserts a declared glob still matches a tracked file, not that a required glob is still declared.

## Why it needs a new mechanism

`SELF_TASK_EXPECTED_GLOBS` already pins a gate's inputs, but as an **exact match** — fine for `repo:input-liveness`, whose entire input list is the single glob `**/*`. `repo:affected-smoke`'s list is ~20 entries and legitimately grows every time a gate keys on a new directory, so an exact-match pin would red on every honest addition.

What is wanted is a **containment** variant: assert that a named set of load-bearing globs is still present, while allowing the rest of the list to change freely. Candidate required set: `moon.yml`, `.moon/**/*`, `ci/affected-graph/**/*`, `ci/actionlint/**/*`, `ci/release-parity/**/*`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `CLAUDE.md`.

## Scope

Add the containment check to `ci_targets.py` alongside `check_gate_inputs`, with its own fixtures, and decide where it runs. Note the self-reference: a check that lives inside `repo:affected-smoke` and asserts `repo:affected-smoke`'s own inputs is the sole judge of its own reachability. The repo's established answer is a second, independently scheduled copy — `ci/actionlint/run.sh` (`inputs: ['**/*']`) already holds checks 8/8b/8c/8d for exactly this reason, so the containment assertion probably belongs **there**, mirroring `ci_targets.py`'s constant, rather than in `ci_targets.py` alone.

Likely wants to land with <issue id="27012e9a-9932-4bea-92e4-3c6c01e84054" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-572/ci-script-pin-the-three-remaining-self-scheduled-gates-in-self">SMA-572</issue>, which needs `repo:affected-smoke`'s inputs pinned as part of script-pinning it.

## Verification

Delete each required glob in turn from `repo:affected-smoke`'s `inputs`; confirm the guarding gate exits non-zero naming it; restore. Include the `moon.yml` case explicitly — that is the self-concealing one, so verify the guard still fires on the very PR that removes it.","projectMilestone":{"id":"0bc8770f-896e-40bc-a156-e0f92b23faf1","name":"MVP"},"priority":{"value":3,"name":"Medium"},"url":"https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-573/ci-pin-that-repoaffected-smoke-still-declares-the-inputs-every-ci","gitBranchName":"feature/sma-573-ci-pin-that-repoaffected-smoke-still-declares-the-inputs","createdAt":"2026-08-22T14:29:23.404Z","updatedAt":"2026-08-28T09:56:44.277Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":"2026-08-28T09:56:44.261Z","canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"status":"In Progress","statusType":"started","labels":["area:ci"],"attachments":[{"id":"0fa0a47c-d656-46b9-963a-35fc69147054","title":"ci: script-pin the remaining self-scheduled gates and pin affected-smoke's reachability (SMA-572, SMA-573)","subtitle":null,"url":"https://github.com/SMK1085/paigasus-core/pull/168"}],"documents":[],"stateHistory":[{"state":{"id":"46bb932e-d4b2-4e1a-8a2a-48ca21321735","name":"Backlog","type":"backlog"},"startedAt":"2026-08-22T14:29:23.404Z","endedAt":"2026-08-28T09:56:44.274Z"},{"state":{"id":"c0917762-f15e-4909-ac0f-851de63723b4","name":"In Progress","type":"started"},"startedAt":"2026-08-28T09:56:44.274Z","endedAt":null}],"createdBy":"Sven Maschek","createdById":"ba6021cb-56c5-43aa-9797-fab3599d7ead","assignee":"Sven Maschek","assigneeId":"ba6021cb-56c5-43aa-9797-fab3599d7ead","project":"Paigasus Polyglot","projectId":"94351cc4-6a23-4c34-a043-2e7f1bfd9ae4","team":"Sven Maschek","teamId":"7178572e-d61f-4cf0-bbcb-4e03c8d9f39e"}

{"id":"SMA-588","title":"iam: twelve Query/Path request extractors answer outside the error envelope","description":"Deferred from <issue id="9a1957cc-7e9d-4298-b1a2-3fd5a78f1df9" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-587/iam-fourteen-http-routes-answer-a-malformed-json-body-outside-the">SMA-587</issue> (see its spec's *Out of scope*). Same class of hole as <issue id="4aee6543-a7cc-481e-8653-5733789b8182" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-586/iam-invalid-prn-is-a-catch-all-sentinel-for-four-unrelated-validation">SMA-586</issue>'s `Path<Uuid>` and <issue id="9a1957cc-7e9d-4298-b1a2-3fd5a78f1df9" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-587/iam-fourteen-http-routes-answer-a-malformed-json-body-outside-the">SMA-587</issue>'s `Json<T>`, third instance.

## The problem

<issue id="9a1957cc-7e9d-4298-b1a2-3fd5a78f1df9" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-587/iam-fourteen-http-routes-answer-a-malformed-json-body-outside-the">SMA-587</issue> made every **body** extractor in `paigasus-iam`'s HTTP adapter answer inside the stable `{"error":{code,message}}` envelope, and added `repo:http-extractor-envelope` to keep it that way. Twelve **non-body** request extractors still escape it:

**Ten** `Query<…>` **bindings** — `?limit=abc` yields axum's plain-text `FailedToDeserializeQueryString` 400 today, with no `error.code`:

| File | Handler |
| -- | -- |
| `api_keys.rs` | list |
| `audit.rs` | list |
| `authz.rs` | list policies |
| `authz.rs` | list role grants |
| `dead_letters.rs` | list |
| `memberships.rs` | list |
| `organizations.rs` | list orgs |
| `organizations.rs` | list teams |
| `service_accounts.rs` | list |
| `teams.rs` | list projects |

**Two** `Path<String>` — not covered by <issue id="4aee6543-a7cc-481e-8653-5733789b8182" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-586/iam-invalid-prn-is-a-catch-all-sentinel-for-four-unrelated-validation">SMA-586</issue>'s `UuidPath` because the segment is not a uuid:

| File | Handler |
| -- | -- |
| `authz.rs` | delete policy (`{id}`) |
| `system_retirement.rs:96` | retire (`{id}`) |

## Why it matters

Same reason as <issue id="9a1957cc-7e9d-4298-b1a2-3fd5a78f1df9" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-587/iam-fourteen-http-routes-answer-a-malformed-json-body-outside-the">SMA-587</issue>: <issue id="ee3dc868-8b58-4ae6-be26-cf4ec9e39783" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-508/ts-paigasussdk-connect-es-grpc-clients-and-error-mapping">SMA-508</issue>'s `@paigasus/sdk` (AC2) branches on `(domain, reason)` and never on message text. A plain-text body has no `reason` to branch on — the SDK cannot parse it into its error type at all. {"id":"SMA-551","title":"repo: gate that ci.yml's moon ci target list and CLAUDE.md's documented one stay in sync","description":"Split out of [SMA-538](<https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-538>) at its final whole-branch review, which found the second instance of this drift.

## The hazard

Two lists name the repo-level Moon gates, and only one of them is authoritative:

* `.github/workflows/ci.yml:215` — the `T=(...)` array actually passed to `moon ci`. **This is what runs.**
* `CLAUDE.md:62-68` — the "run the full graph like CI does" command a developer (or an agent) copies before pushing.

`moon ci` with explicit targets runs **only** the ids it is given, so a gate missing from `ci.yml` does not run in CI no matter what any doc says. Nothing checks the two against each other.

## It has now drifted twice, in both directions

1. `ci.yml` carried the `:release-parity*` gates while `CLAUDE.md` omitted them — recorded as a gotcha in the session memory for <issue id="061db95b-0e21-4e81-a147-ef9bcfe0dbab" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-445/m4-api-keys-and-service-accounts">SMA-445</issue>, i.e. the documented command was *weaker* than CI.
2. <issue id="27ef4e34-923c-4296-ad15-6e9a69adf9e7" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-538/iam-consolidate-the-11-duplicated-docker-skip-policy-copies-and-stop">SMA-538</issue> added `repo:iam-docker-policy-single-site` to `CLAUDE.md`'s list but not to `ci.yml`'s array. **The gate never ran in CI**, so the acceptance criterion it existed to make durable (exactly one definition of the Docker-skip policy) was unprotected on `main` — a twelfth copy could have merged green. Fixed in `115e6f9`.

Direction 2 is the dangerous one: a gate that exists, passes locally, and is documented, but is absent from the only list that matters.

**It is also self-masking. **<issue id="27ef4e34-923c-4296-ad15-6e9a69adf9e7" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-538/iam-consolidate-the-11-duplicated-docker-skip-policy-copies-and-stop">SMA-538</issue>'s own pre-push verification ran the `CLAUDE.md` command — a *superset* of CI's — and went 28/28 green, which actively hid the omission. Any verification driven by the documented list cannot detect that the executed list is missing something.

## Proposal

A `repo:`-scoped Moon gate that extracts both lists and diffs them, modelled on the existing single-site gates (`repo:redis-connect-single-site`, `repo:iam-docker-policy-single-site`) — same shape: narrow `inputs:`, explicit exit codes, and a non-empty control so a parsing change cannot make it pass while guarding nothing.

Sketch:

```bash
ci_targets="$(grep -oE '^\s*T=\(([^)]*)\)' .github/workflows/ci.yml | grep -oE ':[a-z0-9-]+' | sort -u)"
doc_targets="$(sed -n '/run the full graph like CI does/,/--include-relations/p' CLAUDE.md | grep -oE ':[a-z0-9-]+' | sort -u)"
```

then fail on any asymmetric difference, printing which side is missing which target.

Both extractions are brittle against reformatting, which is exactly why the control matters: if either list parses to empty, the gate must `exit 2` ("the guard is not guarding anything"), never pass. `repo:redis-connect-single-site` already establishes that idiom.

Worth considering while implementing: whether `CLAUDE.md` should stop carrying a hand-maintained copy at all and instead point at `ci.yml` as the single source. That removes the drift by construction rather than gating it — but costs the copy-pasteable command, which is the reason the doc line exists. A gate keeps both properties; decide during design.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A `repo:` gate fails when a target is present in `ci.yml`'s `T=(...)` but absent from `CLAUDE.md`'s documented command, and vice versa.
2. It fails loudly (`exit 2`, distinct from a real drift) if either list extracts to empty — a parsing break must not read as "in sync".
3. Proven to red: plant a target on one side only, observe the failure naming it, restore.
4. Narrow `inputs:` so it runs on changes to `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and `CLAUDE.md`, not on every change to the tree.
5. Added to **both** lists it guards, and passing on `main`.

AC 5 is not a joke — a parity gate omitted from `ci.yml` would reproduce the exact defect it exists to prevent.

## Out of scope

The `prebuild.yml` workflow, which runs a napi-only matrix and shares no target list with these two.","projectMilestone":{"id":"0bc8770f-896e-40bc-a156-e0f92b23faf1","name":"MVP"},"priority":{"value":3,"name":"Medium"},"url":"https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-551/repo-gate-that-ciymls-moon-ci-target-list-and-claudemds-documented-one","gitBranchName":"feature/sma-551-repo-gate-that-ciymls-moon-ci-target-list-and-claudemds","createdAt":"2026-08-18T21:31:56.440Z","updatedAt":"2026-08-23T16:06:13.251Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":null,"canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"status":"Backlog","statusType":"backlog","labels":["area:docs","area:ci"],"attachments":[],"documents":[],"stateHistory":[{"state":{"id":"46bb932e-d4b2-4e1a-8a2a-48ca21321735","name":"Backlog","type":"backlog"},"startedAt":"2026-08-18T21:31:56.440Z","endedAt":null}],"createdBy":"Sven Maschek","createdById":"ba6021cb-56c5-43aa-9797-fab3599d7ead","project":"Paigasus Polyglot","projectId":"94351cc4-6a23-4c34-a043-2e7f1bfd9ae4","team":"Sven Maschek","teamId":"7178572e-d61f-4cf0-bbcb-4e03c8d9f39e"}

{"id":"SMA-554","title":"repo: pin ci.yml's moon ci invocation lines as exact literals instead of pattern-matching them","description":"## Context

Follow-up to <issue id="6a49f7cf-951d-433f-b264-6ab7cb728bea" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-541/repo-assert-every-repo-gate-is-actually-wired-into-ciymls-moon-ci">SMA-541</issue>. Its C5 check asserts that `ci.yml`'s `moon ci` invocations are actually handed the whole `T` array. It does this by **matching the invocation line with a regex**, and that approach was bypassed **four separate times** during <issue id="6a49f7cf-951d-433f-b264-6ab7cb728bea" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-541/repo-assert-every-repo-gate-is-actually-wired-into-ciymls-moon-ci">SMA-541</issue>'s own review — each bypass verified real before it was fixed:

1. `moon ci "${T[@]:0:5}" …` — subsetted array (the original motivation)
2. `moon ci --base origin/main "${T[@]:0:5}" …` — subsetted behind a leading flag; seen by neither C5 nor `assert_include_relations`
3. `echo moon ci "${T[@]}" …` and `moon    ci "${T[@]:0:5}" …` — non-executing, and multi-space
4. `moon ci "${T[@]:0:5}" …  # restore "${T[@]}" later` — the expansion supplied by a trailing comment

All five variants are now red and the fixes are sound. **The pattern is the point of this issue**: textual matching of a shell line has a long tail, and each review round produced another member of it. There is no reason to believe the fifth does not exist.

## The evidence for the fix

<issue id="6a49f7cf-951d-433f-b264-6ab7cb728bea" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-541/repo-assert-every-repo-gate-is-actually-wired-into-ciymls-moon-ci">SMA-541</issue> contains a controlled comparison. Two checks match text:

|  | Approach | Bypasses found |
| -- | -- | -- |
| **C4** (`RUN_SH_CALL_SITES`) | exact literals | **1** — and the fix was to make it *more* literal, adding the `\|\| NEG_RC=1` suffix |
| **C5** (`MOON_CI_LINE_RE`) | pattern matching | **4** |

Every C5 bypass was "the pattern did not describe the thing someone wrote". An exact-literal comparison has no tail to enumerate: there is no clever spelling of a string that is not that string.

## Sketch

In `ci/affected-graph/ci_targets.py`:

1. Replace the `MOON_CI_LINE_RE` + `T_ARRAY_EXPANSION` + `_strip_comment` machinery with an exact expected-literal set for the two invocation lines (including indentation).
2. Keep `EXPECTED_MOON_CI_INVOCATIONS` — the count floor is what catches a line vanishing entirely, which an exact-match set cannot see on its own.

{"id":"SMA-555","title":"repo: lint ci/**/*.py with ruff — the convention exists but no gate enforces it","description":"## Context

Surfaced during <issue id="6a49f7cf-951d-433f-b264-6ab7cb728bea" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-541/repo-assert-every-repo-gate-is-actually-wired-into-ciymls-moon-ci">SMA-541</issue>. The Python under `ci/` is expected to comply with the repo's Ruff rule set, but **nothing enforces it**: `.moon/tasks/python.yml` runs `uv run ruff check .` scoped to the `py` project, and `ci/affected-graph/*.py` is outside that scope. No other task lints it.

The consequence was live, not hypothetical: `ci/affected-graph/ci_targets.py` was merged through a full review cycle carrying three `RUF005` violations. Nothing in CI would ever have reported them. They were found only because a CodeRabbit *learning* mentioned the convention in passing, and were fixed in <issue id="6a49f7cf-951d-433f-b264-6ab7cb728bea" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-541/repo-assert-every-repo-gate-is-actually-wired-into-ciymls-moon-ci">SMA-541</issue>'s branch.

An unenforced convention is the latent form of the bug this repo keeps filing — <issue id="4b65db83-2db5-4034-a0b3-749000d8fbb6" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-525/repo-gate-workflow-yaml-with-actionlint-a-malformed-paths-filter-fails">SMA-525</issue>, <issue id="108c3e22-01a6-41be-9939-afe49a0b3035" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-534/rust-a-cargolock-only-change-lints-nothing-so-a-dep-bumps-clippy-break">SMA-534</issue>, <issue id="6a49f7cf-951d-433f-b264-6ab7cb728bea" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-541/repo-assert-every-repo-gate-is-actually-wired-into-ciymls-moon-ci">SMA-541</issue> are all "the rule exists, nothing checks it".

## Measured baseline

Against `py/pyproject.toml`'s config (`select = ["E","F","W","I","N","UP","B","A","C4","SIM","TCH","RUF"]`, `line-length = 200`, `ignore = ["E501"]`):

* `ruff check` — both `ci/affected-graph/cargo_moon_parity.py` and `ci_targets.py` pass **today**, so this lands with no cleanup wave.
* `ruff format --check` — **both files would be reformatted**. So the observed convention is *lint rules only*; formatting is not applied to `ci/` Python. Gate `check`, not `format`, unless you decide otherwise — reformatting both files is a separate call with real diff churn.

## Sketch

1. Add a repo-level Moon task (e.g. `repo:ruff-ci`) running `ruff check` over `ci/**/*.py`, reusing `py/pyproject.toml`'s config so there is one rule set rather than two.
2. Narrow `inputs` to `ci/**/*.py` plus the config file and `.prototools`/`py/uv.lock` — whatever pins the ruff version — so the gate re-keys when the rules or the tool move, not on every change.
3. Add it to `ci.yml`'s `T=(…)` **and** to CLAUDE.md's marker-delimited full-graph command. <issue id="6a49f7cf-951d-433f-b264-6ab7cb728bea" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-541/repo-assert-every-repo-gate-is-actually-wired-into-ciymls-moon-ci">SMA-541</issue>'s gate now fails the build if you forget either, which is a pleasant way to find out this issue is done.

## Acceptance criteria

* A Ruff violation in any file under `ci/` fails CI.
* The gate uses the same rule set as `py/`, not a second copy.
* Both existing `ci/affected-graph/*.py` files pass on an unmutated tree.
* The new task is in `T` and in CLAUDE.md's documented command (enforced by `repo:affected-smoke`).
* Whether `ruff format` should also apply to `ci/` is decided explicitly and recorded, rather than left ambiguous.","projectMilestone":{"id":"0bc8770f-896e-40bc-a156-e0f92b23faf1","name":"MVP"},"priority":{"value":3,"name":"Medium"},"url":"https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-555/repo-lint-cipy-with-ruff-the-convention-exists-but-no-gate-enforces-it","gitBranchName":"feature/sma-555-repo-lint-cipy-with-ruff-the-convention-exists-but-no-gate","createdAt":"2026-08-19T14:52:02.124Z","updatedAt":"2026-08-23T16:05:06.857Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":null,"canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"status":"Backlog","statusType":"backlog","labels":[],"attachments":[],"documents":[],"stateHistory":[{"state":{"id":"46bb932e-d4b2-4e1a-8a2a-48ca21321735","name":"Backlog","type":"backlog"},"startedAt":"2026-08-19T14:52:02.124Z","endedAt":null}],"createdBy":"Sven Maschek","createdById":"ba6021cb-56c5-43aa-9797-fab3599d7ead","project":"Paigasus Polyglot","projectId":"94351cc4-6a23-4c34-a043-2e7f1bfd9ae4","team":"Sven Maschek","teamId":"7178572e-d61f-4cf0-bbcb-4e03c8d9f39e"}

{"id":"SMA-539","title":"repo: lint the inline bash in workflows (pinned shellcheck)","description":"## Context

Follow-up to <issue id="4b65db83-2db5-4034-a0b3-749000d8fbb6" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-525/repo-gate-workflow-yaml-with-actionlint-a-malformed-paths-filter-fails">SMA-525</issue> (limitation L3), which added the `repo:actionlint` gate.

actionlint shells out to `shellcheck` for `run:` blocks whenever it finds one on PATH. <issue id="4b65db83-2db5-4034-a0b3-749000d8fbb6" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-525/repo-gate-workflow-yaml-with-actionlint-a-malformed-paths-filter-fails">SMA-525</issue> **disabled that explicitly** (`-shellcheck= -pyflakes=`) because leaving it opportunistic makes the gate's strictness a property of the host: 0.11.0 via homebrew locally, whatever `ubuntu-latest` currently ships in CI, possibly nothing on a fresh box. An issue whose whole purpose was making a silent failure loud should not ship a sub-check that varies by machine.

So `ci.yml` and `prebuild.yml` carry roughly 120 lines of unlinted inline bash — including `sudo rm -rf /usr/local/lib/android /usr/share/dotnet …` in ci.yml's disk-reclaim step.

## Why this is not just "pin shellcheck"

Pinning it via proto was considered and rejected in <issue id="4b65db83-2db5-4034-a0b3-749000d8fbb6" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-525/repo-gate-workflow-yaml-with-actionlint-a-malformed-paths-filter-fails">SMA-525</issue>'s D2 for a concrete reason: as of 2026-08-16 the `v0.11.0` release publishes **13 archives and no checksums asset**. A `.proto/plugins/shellcheck.toml` would therefore be the first vendored tool in this repo downloaded without integrity verification — a posture regression in a repo that pins action SHAs, runs osv-scanner, and enforces cargo-deny.

That trade deserves its own decision rather than riding along on an unrelated issue.

## Options to weigh

* Pin via proto anyway, accepting an unchecksummed download (and say so explicitly in the plugin header).
* Pin a checksum by hand in the vendored plugin, if proto's TOML schema allows a literal digest.
* Install shellcheck in CI only, from a checksummed source, and keep the local gate shellcheck-free — accepting the local/CI divergence but making it deliberate and documented.
* Leave it disabled and lint the inline bash a different way (extract the long `run:` blocks into `ci/*.sh` files, which the existing tooling already covers).

The last option may be the best of them: `ci/actionlint/run.sh` and `ci/osv/run.sh` already prove that extracted scripts get shellchecked properly.

## Acceptance criteria

* The inline bash in `.github/workflows/**` is linted by something deterministic — same result on a dev box and in CI.
* Whatever is chosen, the integrity story is written down where the next person will find it.
* No new unchecksummed download lands without an explicit, commented justification.","projectMilestone":{"id":"0bc8770f-896e-40bc-a156-e0f92b23faf1","name":"MVP"},"priority":{"value":3,"name":"Medium"},"url":"https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-539/repo-lint-the-inline-bash-in-workflows-pinned-shellcheck","gitBranchName":"feature/sma-539-repo-lint-the-inline-bash-in-workflows-pinned-shellcheck","createdAt":"2026-08-16T20:31:00.030Z","updatedAt":"2026-08-23T16:07:08.597Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":null,"canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"status":"Backlog","statusType":"backlog","labels":[],"attachments":[],"documents":[],"stateHistory":[{"state":{"id":"46bb932e-d4b2-4e1a-8a2a-48ca21321735","name":"Backlog","type":"backlog"},"startedAt":"2026-08-16T20:31:00.030Z","endedAt":null}],"createdBy":"Sven Maschek","createdById":"ba6021cb-56c5-43aa-9797-fab3599d7ead","project":"Paigasus Polyglot","projectId":"94351cc4-6a23-4c34-a043-2e7f1bfd9ae4","team":"Sven Maschek","teamId":"7178572e-d61f-4cf0-bbcb-4e03c8d9f39e"}

{"id":"SMA-560","title":"repo: the py/ts wrappers' Rust source inputs are the ADR-0005 guarantee and nothing asserts them","description":"Deferred from <issue id="914a9b1a-1be1-4212-9b43-cbb488a8f219" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-528/ci-moon-ci-include-relations-does-not-cascade-tasks-so-no-kernel">SMA-528</issue> (PR 145), where it was explicitly declared out of scope rather than assumed away.

## The gap

<issue id="914a9b1a-1be1-4212-9b43-cbb488a8f219" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-528/ci-moon-ci-include-relations-does-not-cascade-tasks-so-no-kernel">SMA-528</issue> gave every **Rust** crate a `fileGroups.upstreams` and added assertion **A6** (`ci/affected-graph/cargo_moon_parity.py`) holding it to strict equality against Moon's own closure. A6 iterates `language == "rust"` projects only.

The **py/ts wrappers** reach the kernel through hand-written globs instead:

* `ts/packages/paigasus-kernel/moon.yml` — `build` and `test` list `/rs/crates/libs/paigasus-kernel/src/**/*` plus both binding crates' sources (<issue id="d6912833-4353-41e8-8dd2-fad8f144b538" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-420/stand-up-a-ts-kernel-binding-wasmnapi-wire-the-cascade-to-paigasus">SMA-420</issue>/427/546)
* `py/packages/paigasus-kernel/moon.yml` — `test` lists the same for the PyO3 side (<issue id="58443395-4277-44a3-a25b-eec88c6c9053" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-419/wire-paigasus-kernel-py-to-the-pyo3-wheel-uvmaturin-runtime-smoke-test">SMA-419</issue>)

Those globs **are** the ADR-0005 cross-binding guarantee: they are what makes a kernel edit re-run the parity replay in each language. **Nothing asserts them.**

* A6 skips these projects — not Rust.
* A5 (`check_ffi_inputs`) asserts only that FFI-compiling tasks declare the four *workspace-level* files: `rs/Cargo.lock`, `rs/Cargo.toml`, `rs/rust-toolchain.toml`, `.prototools`. It says nothing about the per-crate kernel globs.
* The `kernel->bindings` project case reaches those projects via `--downstream deep` over `dependsOn`, which <issue id="914a9b1a-1be1-4212-9b43-cbb488a8f219" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-528/ci-moon-ci-include-relations-does-not-cascade-tasks-so-no-kernel">SMA-528</issue> established is **not** what confers affectedness.

So deleting `/rs/crates/libs/paigasus-kernel/src/**/*` from `paigasus-kernel-ts:build` leaves every gate green while the ts parity replay stops running on kernel changes — the exact defect shape <issue id="914a9b1a-1be1-4212-9b43-cbb488a8f219" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-528/ci-moon-ci-include-relations-does-not-cascade-tasks-so-no-kernel">SMA-528</issue> fixed for Rust.

Note <issue id="46186b0d-8584-4bad-a3aa-2fe8adb80d71" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-535/py-pytypecheck-does-not-propagate-from-rust-so-a-pyo3-signature-change">SMA-535</issue> already observes that `paigasus-kernel-py:test`'s hand-written inputs are "the only thing that closes the gap". This issue is that those inputs are themselves ungated. <issue id="46186b0d-8584-4bad-a3aa-2fe8adb80d71" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-535/py-pytypecheck-does-not-propagate-from-rust-so-a-pyo3-signature-change">SMA-535</issue>/536 ask to *add* propagation for `typecheck`; this asks to *assert* propagation that already exists.

## Suggested fix

Extend A6's closure check across stacks: any project with a `dependsOn` on a Rust crate must key on that crate's sources. Alternatively add the three tasks' kernel globs to A5's required set with a floor.

Watch for the trap A5 already documents: a *derived* target set that silently shrinks to empty asserts nothing while printing PASS. Whatever shape is chosen needs a `REQUIRED_*` floor, and a negative control asserting the specific violation row rather than mere non-emptiness (see A6's controls, `cargo_moon_parity.py` `self_test()`).

## Second case, same gate

A `buf.gen.yaml` or codegen-plugin-version change alters generated output **without** touching a `.proto`. Measured on <issue id="914a9b1a-1be1-4212-9b43-cbb488a8f219" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-528/ci-moon-ci-include-relations-does-not-cascade-tasks-so-no-kernel">SMA-528</issue>:

```
$ echo "contracts/proto/paigasus/gateway/v1/health.proto" | moon query tasks --affected
contracts:breaking contracts:fmt contracts:generate contracts:lint repo:actionlint repo:input-liveness
```

No `paigasus-proto-rs` task and no consumer task. That is not a live hole for a `.proto` edit, because generated code is committed and *those* files select the consumers. It **is** a hole for a change that regenerates differently without a `.proto` diff. Worth covering in the same pass since it is the same "inputs are the only thing that selects" principle.

## Verification

Delete one of the wrapper globs and confirm the gate reds. Then restore and confirm green. A gate that cannot demonstrate that is not covering anything.","projectMilestone":{"id":"0bc8770f-896e-40bc-a156-e0f92b23faf1","name":"MVP"},"priority":{"value":3,"name":"Medium"},"url":"https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-560/repo-the-pyts-wrappers-rust-source-inputs-are-the-adr-0005-guarantee","gitBranchName":"feature/sma-560-repo-the-pyts-wrappers-rust-source-inputs-are-the-adr-0005","createdAt":"2026-08-20T15:50:57.168Z","updatedAt":"2026-08-23T16:04:33.844Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":null,"canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"status":"Backlog","statusType":"backlog","labels":["area:ci"],"attachments":[],"documents":[],"stateHistory":[{"state":{"id":"46bb932e-d4b2-4e1a-8a2a-48ca21321735","name":"Backlog","type":"backlog"},"startedAt":"2026-08-20T15:50:57.168Z","endedAt":null}],"createdBy":"Sven Maschek","createdById":"ba6021cb-56c5-43aa-9797-fab3599d7ead","project":"Paigasus Polyglot","projectId":"94351cc4-6a23-4c34-a043-2e7f1bfd9ae4","team":"Sven Maschek","teamId":"7178572e-d61f-4cf0-bbcb-4e03c8d9f39e"}

{"id":"SMA-535","title":"py: py:typecheck does not propagate from Rust, so a PyO3 signature change ships unchecked","description":"Found while scoping <issue id="51c53fdd-c04b-4433-ba69-4648444d50f8" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-526/rust-lintfmt-propagate-across-no-moon-edge-so-a-downstream-clippy">SMA-526</issue> (Rust lint propagation). Same silent-hole shape, one stack over. An early draft of the <issue id="51c53fdd-c04b-4433-ba69-4648444d50f8" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-526/rust-lintfmt-propagate-across-no-moon-edge-so-a-downstream-clippy">SMA-526</issue> spec claimed py/ts had "no analogous hole"; that claim argued from *coverage* when the question is *scheduling*, and was wrong.

## The problem

`py:lint`, `py:typecheck` and `py:test` live on the `py` configuration-root project (`.moon/tasks/python.yml`, scoped `layers: ['configuration']`). That project:

* has **no** `dependsOn` to any Rust project, and
* lists **no** `rs/**` **inputs** on any of those tasks.

So a Rust kernel or binding edit schedules **none** of them.

## What currently closes the gap, and how far it actually reaches

Only `paigasus-kernel-py:test`'s hand-written `/rs/...` inputs (`py/packages/paigasus-kernel/moon.yml`). That is **runtime** coverage via pytest, not type coverage.

`py/packages/paigasus-kernel/src/paigasus_kernel/__init__.py` re-exports symbols from the PyO3 module. A signature or type change that pytest does not happen to exercise is a basedpyright finding that never runs on the PR introducing it — it surfaces later, on an unrelated py change.

## Suggested fix

Either give the `py` root project an edge to the binding crates, or add the relevant `/rs/...` inputs to `py:typecheck` the way `paigasus-kernel-py:test` already does for its own inputs. Note `py:typecheck` is whole-tree (<issue id="9130e7c4-448f-4e2a-b196-d89576e149a4" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-401/moon-root-per-package-whole-tree-tasks-lintfmttypechecktest-re-run">SMA-401</issue>), so propagating it is coarse — weigh the cost as in <issue id="51c53fdd-c04b-4433-ba69-4648444d50f8" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-526/rust-lintfmt-propagate-across-no-moon-edge-so-a-downstream-clippy">SMA-526</issue>.

{"id":"SMA-537","title":"rust: build.rs and rustfmt.toml are in no task's inputs, so edits to them re-key nothing","description":"Two pre-existing input gaps found while implementing <issue id="51c53fdd-c04b-4433-ba69-4648444d50f8" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-526/rust-lintfmt-propagate-across-no-moon-edge-so-a-downstream-clippy">SMA-526</issue>. Both are about task **inputs** rather than propagation, so <issue id="51c53fdd-c04b-4433-ba69-4648444d50f8" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-526/rust-lintfmt-propagate-across-no-moon-edge-so-a-downstream-clippy">SMA-526</issue> left them alone — but they mean "correct by construction" would be overclaimed for the Rust task graph as a whole.

## 1. `build.rs` is in no task's inputs

`cargo clippy --all-targets` compiles `build.rs`, and `cargo build` obviously runs it. But `.moon/tasks/rust.yml` declares inputs as `@group(sources)` (`src/**/*`), `@group(tests)` and `Cargo.toml` — none of which match a crate-root `build.rs`.

`rs/crates/bindings/paigasus-node-bindings/build.rs` is therefore in no task's inputs: editing it alone re-keys nothing and schedules nothing.

## 2. `rs/rustfmt.toml` is in no `fmt` task's inputs

`fmt` runs `cargo fmt --check` with inputs `@group(sources)` only. The workspace-level `rs/rustfmt.toml` (which sets `max_width = 200`) is not referenced, so changing the global format configuration invalidates no `fmt` task — the whole tree could silently drift out of compliance with the new config until some unrelated edit re-runs `fmt` on each crate.

Note this is a distinct defect from the `fmt` *propagation* question <issue id="51c53fdd-c04b-4433-ba69-4648444d50f8" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-526/rust-lintfmt-propagate-across-no-moon-edge-so-a-downstream-clippy">SMA-526</issue> considered and deliberately rejected. That rejection was correct — `cargo fmt --check` reads only the crate's own files, so it cannot be broken by an *upstream crate* edit. It can, however, be broken by a *config* edit, which is this issue.

## Suggested fix

Add `build.rs` to the `build`/`test`/`lint` inputs and `/rs/rustfmt.toml` to the `fmt` inputs in `.moon/tasks/rust.yml`. {"id":"SMA-552","title":"rust: --locked is unenforceable across the Moon graph, so a build can silently re-resolve the lockfile","description":"Split out of <issue id="da2c0eef-0d09-4c91-b319-d73df57994c5" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-546/rust-a-dep-bump-still-ships-unlinked-clippy-neither-links-the-cdylibs">SMA-546</issue>, which investigated `--locked` on the three FFI build tasks, measured that it **cannot work at that level**, and deliberately deferred it rather than half-ship it. See the "`--locked` was investigated and deliberately deferred" section of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-17-sma-546-ffi-workspace-inputs-design.md` for the full write-up.

## The claim that does not hold

<issue id="108c3e22-01a6-41be-9939-afe49a0b3035" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-534/rust-a-cargolock-only-change-lints-nothing-so-a-dep-bumps-clippy-break">SMA-534</issue> established the principle: without `--locked`, cargo silently re-resolves and **rewrites** an inconsistent `Cargo.lock`, so a gate no longer proves anything about the resolution the PR actually ships. It made `lint` (`cargo clippy --locked`) enforce that. This repo has already shipped a Dependabot lockfile resolved from 3 of 11 workspace members.

That principle is currently enforced for exactly one compile gate. Everything else in the graph can re-resolve behind it.

## Two independent root causes, both measured

**1. The FFI tools pre-resolve. **`napi build` and `wasm-pack build` each run an **un-flagged** `cargo metadata` before their `cargo build`. That call rewrites a stale lockfile, so the subsequent `cargo build --locked` always finds it fresh and can never fail.

Measured on a worktree with the lock made genuinely stale (a dependency added to `rs/crates/bindings/paigasus-wasm/Cargo.toml`):

| invocation | exit | `rs/Cargo.lock` after |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `cargo build --locked` (control) | 101 — *"cannot update the lock file … because* `--locked` *was passed"* | clean |
| `wasm-pack build … -- --locked` | **0** | **REWRITTEN** |
| `napi build … -- --locked` | **0** | **REWRITTEN** |
| `MATURIN_PEP517_ARGS=--locked uv sync --reinstall-package …` | 101 | clean |

Note the py/maturin path is **already correct** — maturin forwards its cargo options to `cargo metadata` too. Only the two ts tools are affected.

**2. The graph pre-resolves.** Even with a task-local `cargo metadata --locked` fail-fast guard (which does work in isolation — verified in both directions), the shared `build` task in `.moon/tasks/rust.yml` is a plain unflagged `cargo build`, inherited by all thirteen crates and scheduled **ahead** of dependents by `deps: ['^:build']`. It rewrites a stale lock itself, so whether any task-local guard fires is **order-dependent**.

## Why it matters now

`rs/Cargo.lock` became a declared **input** of `paigasus-kernel-ts:{build,test}` and `paigasus-kernel-py:test` in <issue id="da2c0eef-0d09-4c91-b319-d73df57994c5" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-546/rust-a-dep-bump-still-ships-unlinked-clippy-neither-links-the-cdylibs">SMA-546</issue> (and of all thirteen `lint` tasks in <issue id="108c3e22-01a6-41be-9939-afe49a0b3035" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-534/rust-a-cargolock-only-change-lints-nothing-so-a-dep-bumps-clippy-break">SMA-534</issue>). A task that rewrites a file it declares as an input:

* invalidates the hash Moon recorded **before** execution, so the cache key describes a tree that no longer exists; and
* races `repo:deny` (`moon.yml:23`), `repo:wasm-getrandom-free` (`moon.yml:250`) and `repo:nats-permissions` (`moon.yml:229`), which read `rs/Cargo.lock` concurrently in the same `moon ci` graph.

Worst case today is a spurious cache miss rather than a wrong result, which is why this is Medium and not Urgent — but the guarantee <issue id="108c3e22-01a6-41be-9939-afe49a0b3035" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-534/rust-a-cargolock-only-change-lints-nothing-so-a-dep-bumps-clippy-break">SMA-534</issue> set out to establish is currently only partial.

## Options to weigh

1. `--locked` **on the shared Rust** `build` **task** in `.moon/tasks/rust.yml` — closes root cause 2 for all thirteen crates in one line. Consider `test` (`cargo nextest run`) too. Costs: reds any PR whose manifest and lock are out of sync (arguably correct, and matches `lint`), changes local dev ergonomics repo-wide, and re-keys every Rust task.
2. **A repo-scoped** `cargo metadata --locked` **preflight gate** — one cheap check that the lock is consistent, independent of which tasks run. Does not stop a rewrite, only detects the inconsistency.
3. **Accept and document** — record the divergence explicitly so nobody re-derives it. This is the current state, via the <issue id="da2c0eef-0d09-4c91-b319-d73df57994c5" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-546/rust-a-dep-bump-still-ships-unlinked-clippy-neither-links-the-cdylibs">SMA-546</issue> spec.

## Verification notes for whoever picks this up

* To make the lock genuinely stale, add a dependency to a member manifest. `git status --short rs/Cargo.lock` **is the only authoritative check for a rewrite** — do *not* grep the lockfile for the package name, because common crates (`itoa`, etc.) are already present as transitive deps and the grep will mislead you.
* Sending a bogus flag through a tool proves the argument **reaches** cargo; it does **not** prove `--locked` bites. Only the staleness experiment distinguishes them. That mistake is what put a false claim into the <issue id="da2c0eef-0d09-4c91-b319-d73df57994c5" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-546/rust-a-dep-bump-still-ships-unlinked-clippy-neither-links-the-cdylibs">SMA-546</issue> spec in the first place.
* Current `--locked` users, for reference: `lint` (`cargo clippy --locked`) is the only compile gate; `repo:publish-metadata` uses it for `cargo package --list` / `cargo publish --dry-run`; `.github/workflows/prebuild.yml` uses `cargo install --locked` for cargo-zigbuild, which is a tool install rather than a workspace build.","projectMilestone":{"id":"0bc8770f-896e-40bc-a156-e0f92b23faf1","name":"MVP"},"priority":{"value":3,"name":"Medium"},"url":"https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-552/rust-locked-is-unenforceable-across-the-moon-graph-so-a-build-can","gitBranchName":"feature/sma-552-rust-locked-is-unenforceable-across-the-moon-graph-so-a","createdAt":"2026-08-19T07:38:09.122Z","updatedAt":"2026-08-23T16:05:19.182Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":null,"canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"status":"Backlog","statusType":"backlog","labels":["area:deps","area:ci","Bug"],"attachments":[],"documents":[],"stateHistory":[{"state":{"id":"46bb932e-d4b2-4e1a-8a2a-48ca21321735","name":"Backlog","type":"backlog"},"startedAt":"2026-08-19T07:38:09.122Z","endedAt":null}],"createdBy":"Sven Maschek","createdById":"ba6021cb-56c5-43aa-9797-fab3599d7ead","project":"Paigasus Polyglot","projectId":"94351cc4-6a23-4c34-a043-2e7f1bfd9ae4","team":"Sven Maschek","teamId":"7178572e-d61f-4cf0-bbcb-4e03c8d9f39e"}

{"id":"SMA-578","title":"Release activation C: maturin cross-platform wheel matrix for paigasus-py-bindings","description":"Third increment of <issue id="d81426f7-9563-4632-ad1b-b5dd4d0b57c4" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-407/release-activation-000-010-floor-kernelproto-lockstep-wiring-live">SMA-407</issue>, per §7 of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-22-sma-407-release-activation-design.md`.

## The gap

`rs/crates/bindings/paigasus-py-bindings/pyproject.toml` carries a standing caveat: a published **sdist** would not carry `rs/.cargo/config.toml`, whose apple-darwin `-undefined dynamic_lookup` flags the `extension-module` cdylib needs to link. So a macOS consumer building from sdist fails.

The design's answer was "wheels only, no sdist" — but **no maturin wheel matrix exists**. `prebuild.yml`'s 6-leg matrix builds the **napi addon**, not wheels; there is no cibuildwheel or maturin-action anywhere in the repo.

A single-runner build yields one manylinux-x86_64 wheel. With no sdist there is no fallback, so `pip install paigasus-kernel` — which the lockstep pins `==` to `paigasus-py-bindings` — **fails outright on macOS, Windows and linux-aarch64**.

## Scope

Either:

1. **A maturin wheel matrix** (decide the triples; <issue id="639b01a8-3b9b-4521-8ca7-dad37ba37f82" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-428/napi-rs-cross-platform-node-prebuild-matrix-npm-publish-for">SMA-428</issue>'s napi matrix is the shape and the precedent — it settled musl-via-cargo-zigbuild, the macos-13 → macos-15-intel retirement, and the GitHub-bans-JS-actions-in-Alpine-on-arm64 trap), **or**
2. **Publish an sdist and solve the** `rs/.cargo/config.toml` **problem properly** — maturin can include it via `[tool.maturin]` config.

Also in scope: `paigasus-py-bindings/pyproject.toml` has essentially no PyPI metadata (no `description`, `readme`, `license-files`, `authors`, `classifiers`) and the crate dir has no `LICENSE` or `README.md` — contrast `py/packages/paigasus-proto/pyproject.toml:4-17`. Nothing gates PyPI metadata the way `repo:publish-metadata` gates [crates.io](<http://crates.io>); decide whether to extend the gate or accept the asymmetry explicitly.

## Size

Comparable to <issue id="639b01a8-3b9b-4521-8ca7-dad37ba37f82" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-428/napi-rs-cross-platform-node-prebuild-matrix-npm-publish-for">SMA-428</issue>. This is why it is not folded into <issue id="58a95803-beac-456d-90da-1b13eec12279" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-576/release-activation-a-kernel-family-010-floor-repoversion-lockstep-gate">SMA-576</issue>.","projectMilestone":{"id":"0bc8770f-896e-40bc-a156-e0f92b23faf1","name":"MVP"},"priority":{"value":3,"name":"Medium"},"url":"https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-578/release-activation-c-maturin-cross-platform-wheel-matrix-for-paigasus","gitBranchName":"feature/sma-578-release-activation-c-maturin-cross-platform-wheel-matrix-for","createdAt":"2026-08-22T18:25:55.056Z","updatedAt":"2026-08-22T18:26:55.308Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":null,"canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"status":"Backlog","statusType":"backlog","labels":["area:release","area:ci"],"attachments":[],"documents":[],"stateHistory":[{"state":{"id":"46bb932e-d4b2-4e1a-8a2a-48ca21321735","name":"Backlog","type":"backlog"},"startedAt":"2026-08-22T18:25:55.056Z","endedAt":null}],"createdBy":"Sven Maschek","createdById":"ba6021cb-56c5-43aa-9797-fab3599d7ead","project":"Paigasus Polyglot","projectId":"94351cc4-6a23-4c34-a043-2e7f1bfd9ae4","parentId":"SMA-407","team":"Sven Maschek","teamId":"7178572e-d61f-4cf0-bbcb-4e03c8d9f39e"}

The design's answer was "wheels only, no sdist" — but **no maturin wheel matrix exists**. `prebuild.yml`'s 6-leg matrix builds the **napi addon**, not wheels; there is no cibuildwheel or maturin-action anywhere in the repo.

A single-runner build yields one manylinux-x86_64 wheel. With no sdist there is no fallback, so `pip install paigasus-kernel` — which the lockstep pins `==` to `paigasus-py-bindings` — **fails outright on macOS, Windows and linux-aarch64**.

1. **A maturin wheel matrix** (decide the triples; <issue id="639b01a8-3b9b-4521-8ca7-dad37ba37f82" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-428/napi-rs-cross-platform-node-prebuild-matrix-npm-publish-for">SMA-428</issue>'s napi matrix is the shape and the precedent — it settled musl-via-cargo-zigbuild, the macos-13 → macos-15-intel retirement, and the GitHub-bans-JS-actions-in-Alpine-on-arm64 trap), **or**
2. **Publish an sdist and solve the** `rs/.cargo/config.toml` **problem properly** — maturin can include it via `[tool.maturin]` config.

## 1. The tagging boundary — assigned here by the codebase

`.github/workflows/prebuild.yml:244-245` states it outright: *"--tag-style left at default *`lerna` *(inert under dry-run; *<issue id="d81426f7-9563-4632-ad1b-b5dd4d0b57c4" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-407/release-activation-000-010-floor-kernelproto-lockstep-wiring-live">SMA-407</issue> *owns the napi/release-plz tagging boundary + the real --gh-release path)"*.

`napi prepublish` defaults `ghRelease: true` and cuts a GitHub release + tag from `package.json`'s version. release-plz also cuts tags. **Two tools tagging the same repo is precisely the ADR-0011 S3 failure mode** — "the tool owns every tag", singular, and the <issue id="4900dca8-16c8-4891-8156-3de7c54b6e90" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-385/release-plz-isnt-bumping-paigasus-helikon-core-past-010-on-featcore">SMA-385</issue> trap that motivated it.

## 2. `@paigasus/wasm` is not publishable as it stands

`rs/crates/bindings/paigasus-wasm/package.json`:

* `"private": true` — `npm publish` refuses.
* No `publishConfig.access: public`, so a scoped package publishes **restricted** — unlike its sibling `paigasus-node-bindings/package.json:32-34`.
* `files` includes `paigasus_wasm_bg.wasm`, which is **gitignored** (`.gitignore:11` `*.wasm`). Publishing from a fresh checkout ships a package with no wasm binary unless the release job runs `wasm-pack` first.
* No `description` / `repository` / `homepage` / `keywords`.

`@paigasus/node-bindings` shares the `private: true` problem.

## 3. Credentials

Publishing credentials go in `release.yml`, **not **`prebuild.yml` — the latter carries a `pull_request` trigger, and same-repo PRs receive repository secrets, so a contributor with push access could exfiltrate a registry token in a PR that never merges. Prefer npm provenance (`permissions: id-token: write`) over a long-lived token.

## Not in scope

`@paigasus/kernel` / `@paigasus/proto` npm publish — there is no JS emit anywhere in `ts/` (every build task is `tsc --noEmit`), so those need a TypeScript build pipeline first. {"id":"SMA-580","title":"Release activation E: pre-flight checklist + flip PAIGASUS_RELEASE_ENABLED","description":"Final increment of <issue id="d81426f7-9563-4632-ad1b-b5dd4d0b57c4" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-407/release-activation-000-010-floor-kernelproto-lockstep-wiring-live">SMA-407</issue>, per §10 of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-22-sma-407-release-activation-design.md`. Blocked on <issue id="58a95803-beac-456d-90da-1b13eec12279" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-576/release-activation-a-kernel-family-010-floor-repoversion-lockstep-gate">SMA-576</issue>, <issue id="46b1513e-1fb2-4883-a327-9ce7845bd614" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-577/release-activation-b-make-the-proto-family-publishable-absorbs-sma-388">SMA-577</issue>, <issue id="ba4aab77-4580-415f-b6a8-37fc53611bdf" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-578/release-activation-c-maturin-cross-platform-wheel-matrix-for-paigasus">SMA-578</issue>, <issue id="de922f9c-1e93-4869-a2aa-c2e1ad2446dd" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-579/release-activation-d-npm-activation-napirelease-plz-tagging-boundary">SMA-579</issue>.

The single irreversible step. Everything before this is reversible; this is not.

## Pre-flight checklist — all of it, before flipping

- [ ] `paigasus-kernel`, `paigasus-proto`, `paigasus-proto-derive` free on [crates.io](<http://crates.io>)
- [ ] `paigasus-kernel`, `paigasus-proto`, `paigasus-py-bindings` free on PyPI
- [ ] the `@paigasus` npm scope owned by this project
- [ ] **no workspace member name squatted on [crates.io](<http://crates.io>)** — with `git_only` unset, release-plz performs a registry lookup for *every* member name (`paigasus-logging`, `paigasus-observability`, …), so a squatted name would silently become the version-comparison baseline
- [ ] the repository is **public** — `docs/ops/RUNBOOK-go-public.md` documents a flip not yet executed, so every published `repository` / `homepage` URL currently 404s
- [ ] `RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN` **repository secret exists**, issued from the **existing Paigasus bot GitHub App** (reuse it — do not create a second App). It needs `contents: write` + `pull-requests: write` on this repo.
  **Why not the default** `GITHUB_TOKEN`**:** GitHub does not trigger `pull_request` workflows for a PR opened by it, so `moon ci` — the required check on the `Protect main` ruleset — would never run and the release PR could never be merged.
  **Needed earlier than the rest of this checklist.** The `release-pr` job shipped live in <issue id="58a95803-beac-456d-90da-1b13eec12279" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-576/release-activation-a-kernel-family-010-floor-repoversion-lockstep-gate">SMA-576</issue>, and its preflight step makes the whole job **skip cleanly (green)** while the secret is absent. That is deliberate (an unguarded job would have reddened `main` on every push), but it means the release path is silently inert until this is done, with nothing in CI to say so. Create it as soon as <issue id="58a95803-beac-456d-90da-1b13eec12279" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-576/release-activation-a-kernel-family-010-floor-repoversion-lockstep-gate">SMA-576</issue> merges if you want to observe the job at all — the item below depends on it.
- [ ] the `release-pr` job has been observed proposing sane versions on real merges

## Expected first-release behaviour

release-plz's baseline is the [**crates.io**](<http://crates.io>) **registry**, not git tags — `ci/release-parity/ecosystems/release-plz.sh:43` sets `git_only = true` precisely to *avoid* the registry lookup for fixture crates, and `rs/release-plz.toml` sets no `git_only`. For a package absent from the registry, the expected behaviour is to treat it as new and propose the **manifest version** — `0.1.0`, no bump.

So the likely observation is an **empty release PR**, not an over-bump. Decide what acceptance evidence looks like in that case.

## Never

Do not hand-place a `*-vX.Y.Z` tag to seed release-plz's tracking. Manual tags lack the metadata release-plz uses to track releases and silently stop all future bumps — the <issue id="4900dca8-16c8-4891-8156-3de7c54b6e90" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-385/release-plz-isnt-bumping-paigasus-helikon-core-past-010-on-featcore">SMA-385</issue> failure, and the direct motivation for ADR-0011 S3's "the tool owns every tag".

## Rollback reality

[crates.io](<http://crates.io>) supports only `cargo yank` (never delete, never reuse); PyPI supports delete-but-never-reuse; npm supports unpublish within 72 hours only. A wrong publish is a permanent version burn in two of three registries.

## Also here

The ADR-0011 amendment (spec §13), if not already landed with <issue id="58a95803-beac-456d-90da-1b13eec12279" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-576/release-activation-a-kernel-family-010-floor-repoversion-lockstep-gate">SMA-576</issue>.

## Also: a one-line comment fix in release.yml

`.github/workflows/release.yml`'s Checkout step explains *why* an App token is required but does not say **which** App. Add that it reuses the **existing Paigasus bot GitHub App** — so nobody creates a second one while debugging why the job skips.

Not done in <issue id="58a95803-beac-456d-90da-1b13eec12279" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-576/release-activation-a-kernel-family-010-floor-repoversion-lockstep-gate">SMA-576</issue>: it surfaced after CI was already mid-flight on the final commit, and restarting the full matrix (7 prebuild legs + images + `moon ci`) for a comment was poor economics.","projectMilestone":{"id":"0bc8770f-896e-40bc-a156-e0f92b23faf1","name":"MVP"},"priority":{"value":3,"name":"Medium"},"url":"https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-580/release-activation-e-pre-flight-checklist-flip-paigasus-release","gitBranchName":"feature/sma-580-release-activation-e-pre-flight-checklist-flip","createdAt":"2026-08-22T18:26:29.639Z","updatedAt":"2026-08-23T08:27:14.870Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":null,"canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"status":"Backlog","statusType":"backlog","labels":["area:release"],"attachments":[],"documents":[],"stateHistory":[{"state":{"id":"46bb932e-d4b2-4e1a-8a2a-48ca21321735","name":"Backlog","type":"backlog"},"startedAt":"2026-08-22T18:26:29.639Z","endedAt":null}],"createdBy":"Sven Maschek","createdById":"ba6021cb-56c5-43aa-9797-fab3599d7ead","project":"Paigasus Polyglot","projectId":"94351cc4-6a23-4c34-a043-2e7f1bfd9ae4","parentId":"SMA-407","team":"Sven Maschek","teamId":"7178572e-d61f-4cf0-bbcb-4e03c8d9f39e"}

{"id":"SMA-556","title":"py: paigasus-ml and paigasus-workflows declare README.md + LICENSE build inputs that do not exist","description":"## Context

Found while measuring the whole-graph input baseline for <issue id="0ef6ae1f-52d0-43f4-a004-1d58dde354b6" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-553/repo-assert-every-repo-tasks-inputs-still-match-a-file-a-gate-can-be">SMA-553</issue> (recorded as §7 of its design doc).

`.moon/tasks/python-project.yml:27` declares `README.md` and `LICENSE` among the `build` task's inputs, inherited by every python project. For two of them the files **do not exist** — not gitignored, absent:

```
py/packages/paigasus-ml/          -> moon.yml, pyproject.toml, src/
py/packages/paigasus-workflows/   -> moon.yml, pyproject.toml, src/
```

So `moon query projects` reports four declared `inputFiles` with no backing file:

* `paigasus-ml-py:build` :: `py/packages/paigasus-ml/README.md`
* `paigasus-ml-py:build` :: `py/packages/paigasus-ml/LICENSE`
* `paigasus-workflows-py:build` :: `py/packages/paigasus-workflows/LICENSE`
* `paigasus-workflows-py:build` :: `py/packages/paigasus-workflows/README.md`

These are the **only** four untracked file inputs in the entire 119-task graph — every other dead input measured is a speculative convention glob from the language task templates, which are harmless.

## Why it matters

Both packages are PyPI-bound and build with `uv_build` (`build-backend = "uv_build"`). Per <issue id="88063e74-3c5a-46be-9ee6-9e85c7c01426" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-378/add-pypi-publishing-metadata-to-paigasus-proto-and-paigasus-kernel">SMA-378</issue>, `uv_build` **does not auto-glob license files**: a package needs `license-files = ["LICENSE"]` in `pyproject.toml` *and* a real `LICENSE` copy, or the wheel ships no license text at all. Neither package has either.

Latent rather than urgent — no release workflow is wired, and the `[tool.semantic_release]` config in both `pyproject.toml`s is explicitly dormant. But it becomes a real defect the moment either package is published.

## Also a precondition for <issue id="0ef6ae1f-52d0-43f4-a004-1d58dde354b6" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-553/repo-assert-every-repo-tasks-inputs-still-match-a-file-a-gate-can-be">SMA-553</issue>

Its §6 L1 records that widening to the whole graph requires two things: pruning the dead convention globs from the task templates, **and** fixing these four — because they are genuine defects that would red first. This issue is that second half.

## Acceptance criteria

* `py/packages/paigasus-ml/` and `py/packages/paigasus-workflows/` each carry a real `LICENSE` (Apache-2.0, matching the repo root) and a `README.md`.
* Both `pyproject.toml`s declare `license-files = ["LICENSE"]`, per the <issue id="88063e74-3c5a-46be-9ee6-9e85c7c01426" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-378/add-pypi-publishing-metadata-to-paigasus-proto-and-paigasus-kernel">SMA-378</issue> pattern already used by whichever py package got it right.
* Confirm against the SPDX-vs-classifier rule <issue id="88063e74-3c5a-46be-9ee6-9e85c7c01426" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-378/add-pypi-publishing-metadata-to-paigasus-proto-and-paigasus-kernel">SMA-378</issue> recorded: an SPDX `license` expression means the `License ::` trove classifier must be **omitted**, not both supplied.

{"id":"SMA-570","title":"iam/gateway: two doc-and-diagnostics follow-ups from SMA-558's CA bundle","description":"Two minor items surfaced by the local CodeRabbit pass on <issue id="886ff241-446e-4ed6-9c25-f42278138ebe" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-558/iam-a-private-ca-oidc-issuer-is-not-trustable-reqwest-carries-compiled">SMA-558</issue> (owner/repo PR 151) and deliberately deferred rather than fixed there. Both shipped to `main` in `e357f62`. Neither is a defect in behaviour — one is an inaccurate doc claim, the other a diagnosability gap.

## 1. The blast-radius claim is wider than the truth

Four sites say a certificate in `extra_ca_bundle_path` becomes an unconstrained trust anchor for **every outbound HTTPS call the process makes**:

* `rs/crates/services/paigasus-iam/src/config.rs`
* `rs/crates/services/paigasus-gateway/src/config.rs`
* `rs/crates/services/paigasus-iam/src/adapters/oidc/jwks.rs`
* `docs/ops/RUNBOOK-containers.md:142`

That overstates it. The anchors are added to one `reqwest::ClientBuilder`, so they apply only to the client built from that bundle — `HttpJwksFetcher`'s in IAM and `OpenAiClient`'s in the gateway. The `tonic` (gateway → IAM), `async-nats` and `redis` links each build their own TLS config and are unaffected.

The "unconstrained anchor / no `cA` check" half of the claim is **correct** and must stay — that is why the bundle has to hold roots only. Only the *scope* is wrong.

`CLAUDE.md:218` already words this correctly ("Anything in an added bundle becomes an **unconstrained** anchor (no `cA` check)") and needs no change.

Note this errs on the cautious side: it overstates how far trust widens, which is the safe direction to be wrong in. That is why it was not worth blocking the merge.

### Fix

Narrow the four sites to name the client, e.g. "for every request this client makes" rather than "the process". Keep the roots-only guidance intact.

## 2. A valid-base64-but-invalid-DER bundle loses the path in its error

The bundle loader has three failure paths. Two name the config key; the third does not.

* unreadable path → names the key and the io error
* zero certificates parsed → names the key
* **PEM section decodes as base64 but is not valid DER** → surfaces later, inside `builder.build()`, at `jwks.rs:166` / `openai/client.rs:175`, and the message is the generic "failed to build the … HTTP client — this can also mean the platform trust store contains no parseable certificates"

So an operator whose bundle holds one structurally broken certificate is told to go look at the platform trust store, which is not where the problem is. The existing tests (`undecodable_bundle_is_a_boot_error`, `undecodable_ca_bundle_is_a_build_error`) cover the *base64* case, which does fail earlier inside `from_pem_bundle` and is correctly attributed — the DER case is the uncovered one.

### Fix

Have the `build()` error retain the configured bundle path when one is set, while leaving the platform-trust-store wording for the no-bundle case. Both services, kept parallel — they are deliberately duplicated (<issue id="886ff241-446e-4ed6-9c25-f42278138ebe" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-558/iam-a-private-ca-oidc-issuer-is-not-trustable-reqwest-carries-compiled">SMA-558</issue> D7).

## Acceptance criteria

1. The four sites in item 1 scope the claim to the client rather than the process, and keep the unconstrained-anchor / roots-only warning.
2. A bundle containing a PEM certificate with valid base64 but invalid DER produces a boot error naming `authn.extra_ca_bundle_path` / `upstream.openai.extra_ca_bundle_path`, not only the generic build message.
3. A test covers that case in both services, asserting the message names the config key — distinct from the existing base64 tests, which fail on a different path.
4. The no-bundle platform-trust-store message is unchanged.","projectMilestone":{"id":"0bc8770f-896e-40bc-a156-e0f92b23faf1","name":"MVP"},"priority":{"value":4,"name":"Low"},"url":"https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-570/iamgateway-two-doc-and-diagnostics-follow-ups-from-sma-558s-ca-bundle","gitBranchName":"feature/sma-570-iamgateway-two-doc-and-diagnostics-follow-ups-from-sma-558s","createdAt":"2026-08-22T08:15:52.185Z","updatedAt":"2026-08-23T16:07:16.538Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":null,"canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"status":"Backlog","statusType":"backlog","labels":["area:iam","area:ops"],"attachments":[],"documents":[],"stateHistory":[{"state":{"id":"46bb932e-d4b2-4e1a-8a2a-48ca21321735","name":"Backlog","type":"backlog"},"startedAt":"2026-08-22T08:15:52.185Z","endedAt":null}],"createdBy":"Sven Maschek","createdById":"ba6021cb-56c5-43aa-9797-fab3599d7ead","project":"Paigasus Polyglot","projectId":"94351cc4-6a23-4c34-a043-2e7f1bfd9ae4","team":"Sven Maschek","teamId":"7178572e-d61f-4cf0-bbcb-4e03c8d9f39e"}

The bundle loader has three failure paths. Two name the config key; the third does not.

* unreadable path → names the key and the io error
* zero certificates parsed → names the key
* **PEM section decodes as base64 but is not valid DER** → surfaces later, inside `builder.build()`, at `jwks.rs:166` / `openai/client.rs:175`, and the message is the generic "failed to build the … HTTP client — this can also mean the platform trust store contains no parseable certificates"

So an operator whose bundle holds one structurally broken certificate is told to go look at the platform trust store, which is not where the problem is. The existing tests (`undecodable_bundle_is_a_boot_error`, `undecodable_ca_bundle_is_a_build_error`) cover the *base64* case, which does fail earlier inside `from_pem_bundle` and is correctly attributed — the DER case is the uncovered one.

### Fix

Have the `build()` error retain the configured bundle path when one is set, while leaving the platform-trust-store wording for the no-bundle case. Both services, kept parallel — they are deliberately duplicated (<issue id="886ff241-446e-4ed6-9c25-f42278138ebe" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-558/iam-a-private-ca-oidc-issuer-is-not-trustable-reqwest-carries-compiled">SMA-558</issue> D7).

## Acceptance criteria

1. The four sites in item 1 scope the claim to the client rather than the process, and keep the unconstrained-anchor / roots-only warning.
2. A bundle containing a PEM certificate with valid base64 but invalid DER produces a boot error naming `authn.extra_ca_bundle_path` / `upstream.openai.extra_ca_bundle_path`, not only the generic build message.
3. A test covers that case in both services, asserting the message names the config key — distinct from the existing base64 tests, which fail on a different path.
4. content.text:
## What's actually open in MVP

Excluding the Frontend milestone, MVP has **19 open issues**. Two of them are already done, one pair is in flight, and the rest fall into three clean clusters.

### First: two you can close right now

| Issue | Evidence |
|---|---|
| **SMA-388** "Flip paigasus-proto publish=false" | `rs/crates/libs/paigasus-proto/Cargo.toml:32` already says `publish = true` at `version = "0.1.0"`. SMA-577 absorbed it, as its own title says. |
| **SMA-551** "Gate ci.yml's `T` vs CLAUDE.md" | Already implemented by SMA-541. `ci/affected-graph/ci_targets.py:554-732` extracts the marker region, diffs it against `T` **ordered**, checks the flag tail, and hard-fails on an empty region ("the documented full-graph command is gone") — that's AC1–AC5 including the `exit 2` control. |

### And one blocker on your in-flight work

PR **#168** (SMA-572 + SMA-573) is open with **`moon ci` failing**. Those two were already correctly combined. Worth clearing before starting anything that touches `ci_targets.py` — which is most of the CI backlog.

## Recommended next pass — combine SMA-560 + SMA-535 + SMA-537

These three are one idea: *task `inputs` are the only thing that confers affectedness*, applied to three places that still don't have them.

- **SMA-537** (Low) — `build.rs` is in no task's inputs; `rs/rustfmt.toml` is in no `fmt` task's inputs. Two lines in `.moon/tasks/rust.yml`.
- **SMA-535** (Medium) — `py:typecheck` has no `rs/**` inputs, so a PyO3 signature change ships type-unchecked.
- **SMA-560** (Medium) — the py/ts wrappers' hand-written kernel globs *are* the ADR-0005 guarantee, and A6 skips them because it iterates `language == "rust"` only.

**Why combine:** all three edit `.moon/tasks/*.yml` inputs and/or `cargo_moon_parity.py`, and every one of them forces a re-baseline of `ci/affected-graph/run.sh`'s strict-equality expected sets. That re-baseline is the expensive, error-prone part — doing it once instead of three times is the whole saving. Sequentially they'd also each invalidate the previous one's baseline.

Optional fourth: **SMA-536** (ts:typecheck, Frontend milestone) is the exact ts twin of SMA-535 — near-free to fold in.

## Second pass — SMA-555 + SMA-539 (+ SMA-556 rides free)

- **SMA-555** — ruff over `ci/**/*.py`. Measured clean today, so it lands with no cleanup wave.
- **SMA-539** — shellcheck the ~120 lines of inline workflow bash. Its own preferred option ("extract long `run:` blocks into `ci/*.sh`, which existing tooling already covers") makes it structurally the same work as 555.
- **SMA-556** — add `LICENSE`/`README.md` to `paigasus-ml` and `paigasus-workflows`. Trivial, and it's the stated precondition for widening SMA-553's gate beyond the `repo` project.

Both new gates need the identical `T=(…)` + CLAUDE.md-marker wiring ritual, and SMA-541's gate will tell you immediately if you forget either.

**Do not** fold **SMA-554** in here — it rewrites the `MOON_CI_LINE_RE` machinery in `ci_targets.py` and would collide head-on with PR #168. It's a clean solo after #168 merges.

## Highest external value, standalone: SMA-588

Third instance of the error-envelope hole (after SMA-586's `Path<Uuid>` and SMA-587's `Json<T>`). Ten `Query<…>` + two `Path<String>` extractors still answer plain text. I confirmed the gate was pre-built for it — `ci/http-extractor/check.py:50-54` carries the reserved rows:

```python
BANNED = (
    ("Json",  True,  "EnvelopeJson"),
    ("Query", False, None),   # ← this ticket
    ("Path",  False, None),   # ← this ticket
)
```

So it's mostly a flag flip plus three design calls (which reason; generalise `UuidPath`; tighten the `Path` match against `std::path::Path`). It directly unblocks **SMA-508** (`@paigasus/sdk`, High) which branches on `(domain, reason)` and cannot parse a plain-text body at all.

⚠️ **SMA-588 has no milestone.** Given it gates a High Frontend issue, it probably belongs in MVP.

## Release cluster — one thing to do today

input.body:
Closing as already satisfied — implemented by SMA-541, which did not reference this issue, so it stayed open.

Verified on `main` (3f23758) in `ci/affected-graph/ci_targets.py`. Against this issue's ACs:

- **AC1** (fails on asymmetric difference, both directions) — met, and *stronger* than asked: the check is **ordered**, not set-based. `doc_problems()` (~line 717) reports "first divergence at position i", so a reordering also reds, not just a missing entry. It additionally asserts the flag tail (`--base origin/main --include-relations`).
- **AC2** (loud failure, distinct from real drift, if either list extracts empty) — met. The marker parse (~line 554) hard-fails on: not exactly one `<!-- ci-targets:begin -->` / `<!-- ci-targets:end -->` pair, inverted markers, and an empty region ("CLAUDE.md's ci-targets region is empty — the documented full-graph command is gone").
- **AC3** (proven to red) — met; fixtures exist, e.g. `expect_doc_red("no-markers", ...)` at ~line 1037.
- **AC4** (narrow `inputs`) — met; it runs inside `repo:affected-smoke`, which lists both `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and `CLAUDE.md`.
- **AC5** ("added to both lists it guards") — met transitively: `:affected-smoke` is in `ci.yml`'s `T=(…)` at line 214 and in CLAUDE.md's marker-delimited command.

The design note in the issue ("whether CLAUDE.md should stop carrying a hand-maintained copy at all") was resolved the other way — the copy stays, and the gate keeps it honest. That is the option this issue argued preserved both properties.

Worth noting the follow-up **SMA-573** exists precisely because this mechanism's reachability depends on `repo:affected-smoke`'s own `inputs` being intact, which nothing yet pins. That is the remaining gap in this area, and it is already in flight on PR #168.

{"id":"SMA-388","title":"Flip paigasus-proto publish=false once generated code lands","description":"The `paigasus-proto` Rust crate is scaffolded in <issue id="2651acfc-55de-45c6-9976-fede71901b0a" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-360/bootstrap-contracts-proto-workspace-with-buf-scaffold">SMA-360</issue> with `publish = false` (empty, no generated code yet). Per the open-core release strategy (Polyglot Monorepo Scoping §4), `paigasus-proto` is crates.io-bound — `paigasus-cloud` consumes it as a published dependency. An un-flipped `publish = false` would silently exclude it from the release pipeline.

Mirror the kernel crate's pattern (`TODO(SMA-376)`): the <issue id="2651acfc-55de-45c6-9976-fede71901b0a" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-360/bootstrap-contracts-proto-workspace-with-buf-scaffold">SMA-360</issue> `Cargo.toml` TODO should cite this issue.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `paigasus-proto` `Cargo.toml` flips `publish = true` (and picks a real 0.x version) once it carries release-worthy generated code.
- [ ] Crate is wired into `release.yml`'s `cargo publish` dependency order.
