{"id":"SMA-551","title":"repo: gate that ci.yml's moon ci target list and CLAUDE.md's documented one stay in sync","description":"Split out of [SMA-538](<https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-538>) at its final whole-branch review, which found the second instance of this drift.

## The hazard

Two lists name the repo-level Moon gates, and only one of them is authoritative:

* `.github/workflows/ci.yml:215` — the `T=(...)` array actually passed to `moon ci`. **This is what runs.**
* `CLAUDE.md:62-68` — the "run the full graph like CI does" command a developer (or an agent) copies before pushing.

`moon ci` with explicit targets runs **only** the ids it is given, so a gate missing from `ci.yml` does not run in CI no matter what any doc says. Nothing checks the two against each other.

## It has now drifted twice, in both directions

1. `ci.yml` carried the `:release-parity*` gates while `CLAUDE.md` omitted them — recorded as a gotcha in the session memory for <issue id="061db95b-0e21-4e81-a147-ef9bcfe0dbab" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-445/m4-api-keys-and-service-accounts">SMA-445</issue>, i.e. the documented command was *weaker* than CI.
2. <issue id="27ef4e34-923c-4296-ad15-6e9a69adf9e7" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-538/iam-consolidate-the-11-duplicated-docker-skip-policy-copies-and-stop">SMA-538</issue> added `repo:iam-docker-policy-single-site` to `CLAUDE.md`'s list but not to `ci.yml`'s array. **The gate never ran in CI**, so the acceptance criterion it existed to make durable (exactly one definition of the Docker-skip policy) was unprotected on `main` — a twelfth copy could have merged green. Fixed in `115e6f9`.

Direction 2 is the dangerous one: a gate that exists, passes locally, and is documented, but is absent from the only list that matters.

**It is also self-masking. **<issue id="27ef4e34-923c-4296-ad15-6e9a69adf9e7" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-538/iam-consolidate-the-11-duplicated-docker-skip-policy-copies-and-stop">SMA-538</issue>'s own pre-push verification ran the `CLAUDE.md` command — a *superset* of CI's — and went 28/28 green, which actively hid the omission. Any verification driven by the documented list cannot detect that the executed list is missing something.

## Proposal

A `repo:`-scoped Moon gate that extracts both lists and diffs them, modelled on the existing single-site gates (`repo:redis-connect-single-site`, `repo:iam-docker-policy-single-site`) — same shape: narrow `inputs:`, explicit exit codes, and a non-empty control so a parsing change cannot make it pass while guarding nothing.

Sketch:

```bash
ci_targets="$(grep -oE '^\s*T=\(([^)]*)\)' .github/workflows/ci.yml | grep -oE ':[a-z0-9-]+' | sort -u)"
doc_targets="$(sed -n '/run the full graph like CI does/,/--include-relations/p' CLAUDE.md | grep -oE ':[a-z0-9-]+' | sort -u)"
```

then fail on any asymmetric difference, printing which side is missing which target.

Both extractions are brittle against reformatting, which is exactly why the control matters: if either list parses to empty, the gate must `exit 2` ("the guard is not guarding anything"), never pass. `repo:redis-connect-single-site` already establishes that idiom.

Worth considering while implementing: whether `CLAUDE.md` should stop carrying a hand-maintained copy at all and instead point at `ci.yml` as the single source. That removes the drift by construction rather than gating it — but costs the copy-pasteable command, which is the reason the doc line exists. A gate keeps both properties; decide during design.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A `repo:` gate fails when a target is present in `ci.yml`'s `T=(...)` but absent from `CLAUDE.md`'s documented command, and vice versa.
2. It fails loudly (`exit 2`, distinct from a real drift) if either list extracts to empty — a parsing break must not read as "in sync".
3. Proven to red: plant a target on one side only, observe the failure naming it, restore.
4. Narrow `inputs:` so it runs on changes to `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and `CLAUDE.md`, not on every change to the tree.
5. Added to **both** lists it guards, and passing on `main`.

AC 5 is not a joke — a parity gate omitted from `ci.yml` would reproduce the exact defect it exists to prevent.

## Out of scope

The `prebuild.yml` workflow, which runs a napi-only matrix and shares no target list with these two.","projectMilestone":{"id":"0bc8770f-896e-40bc-a156-e0f92b23faf1","name":"MVP"},"priority":{"value":3,"name":"Medium"},"url":"https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-551/repo-gate-that-ciymls-moon-ci-target-list-and-claudemds-documented-one","gitBranchName":"feature/sma-551-repo-gate-that-ciymls-moon-ci-target-list-and-claudemds","createdAt":"2026-08-18T21:31:56.440Z","updatedAt":"2026-08-28T11:46:27.084Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":"2026-08-28T11:46:27.076Z","startedAt":null,"canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"status":"Done","statusType":"completed","labels":["area:docs","area:ci"],"attachments":[],"documents":[],"createdBy":"Sven Maschek","createdById":"ba6021cb-56c5-43aa-9797-fab3599d7ead","project":"Paigasus Polyglot","projectId":"94351cc4-6a23-4c34-a043-2e7f1bfd9ae4","team":"Sven Maschek","teamId":"7178572e-d61f-4cf0-bbcb-4e03c8d9f39e"}

# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
name: release

# Only the RELEASE-PR half is live (SMA-576). The release job — tags + registry publishes —
# lands with SMA-580 behind `vars.PAIGASUS_RELEASE_ENABLED`. Nothing here publishes.
on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main

# release-plz force-updates its PR branch on every run, so two rapid merges to main would
# race. Do NOT cancel in progress: a cancelled run can leave the branch half-written.
concurrency:
  group: release-pr
  cancel-in-progress: false

# Least privilege for the auto GITHUB_TOKEN, matching every other workflow here: it is never
# used for the push/PR below (that goes through secrets.RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN — see Checkout).
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  release-pr:
    name: release PR
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      # RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN does not exist yet (a human must create it — see the workflow's
      # own doc). A job-level `if:` cannot see whether it's set: per GitHub's own context-
      # availability table, `jobs.<job_id>.if` only sees github/needs/vars/inputs, never
      # secrets. A step's `if:`/`env:` CAN see secrets, so every step below is individually
      # guarded on this step's output instead. Left unconfigured, this makes the whole job
      # skip cleanly (green) on every push to main instead of failing loudly forever.
      - name: Check for the release-plz token
        id: preflight
        env:
          TOKEN_SET: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN != '' }}
        run: |
          echo "configured=$TOKEN_SET" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          if [ "$TOKEN_SET" != "true" ]; then
            echo "::notice::RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN is not set — skipping the release-PR job until a human creates it (see release.yml)."
          fi

      - name: Checkout
        if: steps.preflight.outputs.configured == 'true'
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1  # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # persist-credentials: false, matching every other checkout in this repo
          # (artipacked hardening). An earlier revision persisted the App token here so the
          # stamping step could push — but `actions/checkout` writes that credential into
          # the local git config for the WHOLE job, which handed a write-capable token to
          # four steps that have no business with it (setup-toolchain, proto install,
          # moon setup, pnpm install). A compromised action or transitive dependency in any
          # of them could have used it before release work even began.
          #
          # The token now reaches only the two steps that genuinely need it, via their own
          # `env:` — release-plz (GIT_TOKEN) and the stamping step (which authenticates its
          # fetch/push through an explicit remote URL rather than ambient git config).
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Set up proto + Moon
        if: steps.preflight.outputs.configured == 'true'
        uses: moonrepo/setup-toolchain@261c62cb5b0f580c7be7c8cd0f023a2e96756095  # v0
        with:
          # Don't cache the proto/Moon toolchain dir: a restored ~/.proto carries stale
          # setup-state that makes `moon setup` skip installing node/pnpm (their shims
          # then don't exist). Reinstall fresh each run (matches ci.yml/prebuild.yml).
          cache: false

      # release-plz is proto-pinned like every other CLI this repo depends on
      # (.prototools, .proto/plugins/release-plz.toml) — install the pinned binary
      # directly rather than through a third-party GitHub Action, which would resolve
      # its own, unpinned release-plz build. Narrow install (not a bare `proto install`):
      # this job needs none of actionlint/buf/deny/machete/nextest/promtool/wasm-pack.
      - name: Install pinned release-plz CLI
        if: steps.preflight.outputs.configured == 'true'
        run: proto install release-plz

      - name: Install Moon-managed toolchains (node, pnpm, rust, python, uv)

# rs/release-plz.toml and rs/Cargo.toml without --config/--manifest-path flags.
      #
      # `--output json` always prints one line, `{"prs": [...]}`, with 0 or 1 elements —
      # verified against the pinned 0.3.158 source
      # (release_plz_core::command::release_pr::release_pr returns Option<ReleasePr>;
      # main.rs wraps None as `[]`, Some(pr) as `[pr]`). Each element carries head_branch/
      # base_branch/html_url/number/releases (the ReleasePr struct) — the CLI's own --help
      # only promises "prints the branch, URL and number", so this was confirmed by reading
      # the source at the exact pinned tag, not assumed from the docs.
      - name: Open or update the release PR
        id: release_pr
        if: steps.preflight.outputs.configured == 'true'
        working-directory: rs
        env:
          GIT_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          OUT="$(release-plz release-pr --output json)"
          echo "$OUT"
          echo "json=$OUT" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      # release-plz does ALL of its work — version bumps, changelog, branch creation, push —
      # inside a private copy under a tempdir
      # (release_plz_core::command::release_pr::copy_to_temp_dir, confirmed by reading the
      # pinned 0.3.158 source and independently measured: a throwaway clone's HEAD and
      # working tree were untouched after a real `release-pr` run). This checkout's `main`
      # is therefore NEVER the branch to act on — the branch comes only from the JSON above,
      # never from `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` (which would still read "main" here and
      # push straight to it).
      - name: Stamp the non-Cargo manifests onto the release PR branch
        if: steps.preflight.outputs.configured == 'true'
        env:
          PR_JSON: ${{ steps.release_pr.outputs.json }}
          # Scoped to this step only. The checkout sets persist-credentials: false, so there
          # are no ambient git credentials — the fetch and push below authenticate through an
          # explicit remote URL built from this value. GitHub masks the secret in logs, and
          # the URL is never written to git config (no `remote set-url`), so it does not
          # outlive the commands themselves.
          GH_TOKEN_FOR_PUSH: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          PR_COUNT="$(printf '%s' "$PR_JSON" | jq '.prs | length')"
          if [ "$PR_COUNT" -eq 0 ]; then
            echo "release-plz: no release PR needed (every releasable package is already" \
                 "at its proposed version) — nothing to stamp"
            exit 0
          fi
          BRANCH="$(printf '%s' "$PR_JSON" | jq -r '.prs[0].head_branch')"
          AUTH_REMOTE="REDACTED"

          git fetch "$AUTH_REMOTE" "$BRANCH"
          git checkout -B "$BRANCH" FETCH_HEAD

          bash ci/version-lockstep/run.sh --write

          if git diff --quiet; then
            echo "version-lockstep: nothing to stamp"
            exit 0
          fi
          git config user.name  "paigasus-release[bot]"
          git config user.email "paigasus-release[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git add -A
          git commit -m "chore(rs): stamp the non-Cargo manifests to the release version"
          git push "$AUTH_REMOTE" "HEAD:$BRANCH"

content.text:
I read `release.yml` before answering, and there's a problem with the issue's instruction that you should decide on first.

## The blocker: the workflow can't consume an App token as written

SMA-580's checklist says to issue the token "from the **existing Paigasus bot GitHub App**". But `release.yml` uses the secret as a **raw, static token string** in two places:

- `release.yml:109` — `GIT_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN }}`
- `release.yml:133` → `REDACTED`

A GitHub App **installation token expires after one hour**. It cannot be stored as a repository secret. Minting one requires an `actions/create-github-app-token` step in the workflow — and I verified there is none:

```
$ grep -rn "create-github-app-token\|APP_ID\|PRIVATE_KEY" .github/workflows/
(no matches)

$ grep -rhoE "secrets\.[A-Z_]+" .github/ | sort -u
secrets.RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN
```

So "create the secret" is a one-command job **only** if you use a PAT. Using the App is a workflow change plus two different secrets.

The `x-access-token:` username at line 133 and the hardcoded `paigasus-release[bot]` committer at lines 154-155 both look like the App path was the design intent — it just never got the minting step, presumably because SMA-576 shipped the job inert.

I also couldn't confirm the App exists from here — your `gh` token has scopes `gist, read:org, repo`, and listing App installations needs more, so that's something you'll have to eyeball in the browser.

## Path A — GitHub App (matches the intent; needs a small PR)

1. **Find the App.** `github.com/settings/apps` (or the org's Developer settings). Note its **App ID**. If it doesn't exist, create one — don't create a *second* one if it does.
2. **Repository permissions:** Contents → *Read and write*; Pull requests → *Read and write*. (Metadata: Read comes automatically.)
3. **Install it** on `SMK1085/paigasus-core`.
4. **Generate a private key** → downloads a `.pem`.
5. **Store two secrets** (run these yourself so the key never lands in my transcript):
   ```
   ! gh secret set PAIGASUS_BOT_APP_ID --body "<the app id>"
   ! gh secret set PAIGASUS_BOT_PRIVATE_KEY < ~/Downloads/<app>.private-key.pem
   ```
6. **Edit `release.yml`** — add a SHA-pinned `create-github-app-token` step (guarded by the preflight, per the file's existing pattern), repoint the preflight to key on `secrets.PAIGASUS_BOT_APP_ID != ''`, and feed the step's `outputs.token` into the two `env:` sites.
7. `rm` the `.pem`.

Trade-off: no long-lived credential, auto-expiring token, commits genuinely attributed to the bot. Costs a reviewed PR against a file whose comments are unusually careful about credential scope.

## Path B — fine-grained PAT (works today, zero code change)

1. `github.com/settings/personal-access-tokens/new`
2. Resource owner `SMK1085`; Repository access → **Only select repositories** → `paigasus-core`
3. Repository permissions: Contents → *Read and write*; Pull requests → *Read and write*
4. Set an expiry and put the rotation date in your calendar — this is the failure mode of this path
5. ```
   ! gh secret set RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN
   ```
   (paste at the prompt; avoid `--body`, which lands the token in shell history)

Trade-off: live in ~2 minutes, but a long-lived credential bound to your personal account, in a repo that otherwise pins action SHAs, sets `persist-credentials: false`, and runs osv-scanner + cargo-deny.

Either satisfies SMA-580's actual functional requirement — the reason `GITHUB_TOKEN` is unusable is that PRs it opens don't trigger `pull_request` workflows, so `moon ci` (your required check) would never run and the release PR could never merge. **Both** a PAT and an App installation token do trigger them.

One thing worth knowing before you pick: whichever you choose, the first release PR is expected to be **empty** — release-plz's baseline is the crates.io registry, and at the `0.1.0` floor it proposes the manifest version with no bump.

python3 - <<'PY'
import io, sys
p = ".github/workflows/release.yml"
s = io.open(p, encoding="utf-8").read()
orig = s

def rep(old, new, n=1):
    global s
    c = s.count(old)
    assert c == n, f"expected {n} occurrence(s), found {c}:\n{old[:120]}"
    s = s.replace(old, new)

# A. header comment
rep(
"# used for the push/PR below (that goes through secrets.RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN — see Checkout).",
"# used for the push/PR below (that goes through the App installation token — see \"Mint\").")

# B. preflight + new mint step
rep('''      # RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN does not exist yet (a human must create it — see the workflow's
      # own doc). A job-level `if:` cannot see whether it's set: per GitHub's own context-
      # availability table, `jobs.<job_id>.if` only sees github/needs/vars/inputs, never
      # secrets. A step's `if:`/`env:` CAN see secrets, so every step below is individually
      # guarded on this step's output instead. Left unconfigured, this makes the whole job
      # skip cleanly (green) on every push to main instead of failing loudly forever.
      - name: Check for the release-plz token
        id: preflight
        env:
          TOKEN_SET: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN != '' }}
        run: |
          echo "configured=$TOKEN_SET" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          if [ "$TOKEN_SET" != "true" ]; then
            echo "::notice::RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN is not set — skipping the release-PR job until a human creates it (see release.yml)."
          fi
''',
'''      # The App credentials may not exist yet (a human must create them — see the workflow's
      # own doc). A job-level `if:` cannot see whether a secret is set: per GitHub's own
      # context-availability table, `jobs.<job_id>.if` only sees github/needs/vars/inputs,
      # never secrets. A step's `if:`/`env:` CAN see secrets, so every step below is
      # individually guarded on this step's output instead. Left unconfigured, this makes the
      # whole job skip cleanly (green) on every push to main rather than failing forever.
      #
      # Keyed on the App ID rather than the private key purely because an ID is not itself a
      # credential. Both are required by the mint step below, so a HALF-configured App fails
      # there instead of skipping — which is correct: that is a real misconfiguration, not a
      # "not set up yet".
      - name: Check for the App credentials
        id: preflight
        env:
          APP_ID_SET: ${{ secrets.PAIGASUS_BOT_APP_ID != '' }}
        run: |
          echo "configured=$APP_ID_SET" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          if [ "$APP_ID_SET" != "true" ]; then
            echo "::notice::PAIGASUS_BOT_APP_ID is not set — skipping the release-PR job until a human creates the App secrets (see release.yml)."
          fi

      # An App INSTALLATION token, minted fresh per run and valid for one hour — which is
      # exactly why it cannot be a stored repository secret, and why the earlier
      # RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN shape could only ever have held a long-lived PAT. This job's
      # timeout-minutes: 20 keeps the whole run well inside that hour, so one mint here is
      # enough for both consumers below.
      #
      # Scoped to THIS repository (the action defaults `repositories` to the current repo) and
      # carrying only what the App is granted: contents:write for the stamping push, and
      # pull-requests:write for release-plz opening/updating the PR.
      #
      # The action registers the token as a log mask and revokes it in its post-step, so it
      # does not outlive the run.
      - name: Mint the App installation token
        id: app_token
        if: steps.preflight.outputs.configured == 'true'
        uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1  # v3.2.0
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.PAIGASUS_BOT_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.PAIGASUS_BOT_PRIVATE_KEY }}
''')

# C + D. the two consumers
rep("          GIT_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN }}",
    "          GIT_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app_token.outputs.token }}")
rep("          GH_TOKEN_FOR_PUSH: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN }}",
    "          GH_TOKEN_FOR_PUSH: ${{ steps.app_token.outputs.token }}")

assert "RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN" not in s, "a RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN reference survived"
assert s != orig
io.open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(s)
print("release.yml updated")
PY

**What changed** (4 sites, all in `.github/workflows/release.yml`):

1. **Preflight** now keys on `secrets.PAIGASUS_BOT_APP_ID` instead of `RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN` — same skip-clean-green behaviour, same reason it can't be a job-level `if:`.
2. **New step `app_token`** — `actions/create-github-app-token` pinned to `bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1` (v3.2.0, SHA resolved from the API, matching the repo's pinning convention), guarded by the preflight, placed before Checkout.
3. **`GIT_TOKEN`** (line 134) and **`GH_TOKEN_FOR_PUSH`** (line 158) now read `steps.app_token.outputs.token`.

Both your secrets are in place and named as expected:
```
PAIGASUS_BOT_APP_ID       2026-08-28T11:50:23Z
PAIGASUS_BOT_PRIVATE_KEY  2026-08-28T11:51:12Z
```

**Verified:** `moon run repo:actionlint` passes, and the file parses with the steps in the right order (`preflight` → `app_token` → `Checkout` → …).

Two design notes I baked into the comments:

- **Why the preflight keys on the App ID, not the private key** — an ID isn't itself a credential. The mint step needs *both*, so a half-configured App fails loudly there rather than skipping silently. That's the right split: "not set up yet" skips, "set up wrong" reds.

I left the existing `persist-credentials: false` comment untouched — it already explains why the token reaches only the two steps that need it, and that reasoning holds unchanged (arguably better now, since the token also self-revokes).

Two things I did **not** do, both worth your call:

- **Not committed.** You're on `main`, and the convention is `feature/sma-NNN-<slug>` with a pre-push hook enforcing it. This work sits in SMA-580's checklist, but SMA-580 is the blocked "irreversible flip" issue — so it's either a partial PR on `feature/sma-580-…` or a small new issue. Which do you want?
- **`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-22-sma-576-…md:1120`** still describes the `RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN` shape. I left it — it's a dated record of what SMA-576 planned, not live guidance.

input.title: release: mint the App installation token in-workflow — release.yml cannot consume a stored one
input.description:
Split out of SMA-580, whose checklist requires `RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN` to be "issued from the existing Paigasus bot GitHub App". As shipped, `release.yml` cannot consume such a token.

## The defect

SMA-576 shipped the `release-pr` job reading a **static** secret in two places:

* `release.yml:109` — `GIT_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN }}`
* `release.yml:133` — interpolated into `REDACTED`

A GitHub App **installation token expires after one hour**, so it cannot be stored as a repository secret. Minting one requires an `actions/create-github-app-token` step, and there is none — confirmed by grep across `.github/`, where `secrets.RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN` was the *only* secret the repo referenced at all.

So the shipped shape could only ever have held a long-lived PAT. That is at odds with the surrounding posture (pinned action SHAs, `persist-credentials: false` / artipacked hardening, osv-scanner, cargo-deny) and with the design's own intent — the `x-access-token:` username at line 133 and the hardcoded `paigasus-release[bot]` committer at lines 154-155 are both App-shaped. The minting step was simply never added, presumably because the job shipped inert.

## Why it was invisible

The job's preflight makes it **skip cleanly green** while the secret is absent. That is deliberate and correct (an unguarded job would have reddened `main` on every push), but it means nothing in CI ever exercised the token path, so the missing step could not surface.

## Scope

1. Repoint the preflight to key on `secrets.PAIGASUS_BOT_APP_ID`.
2. Add a SHA-pinned `actions/create-github-app-token` step, guarded by the preflight, before Checkout.
3. Feed `steps.app_token.outputs.token` into both consumers.

The App and its two secrets (`PAIGASUS_BOT_APP_ID`, `PAIGASUS_BOT_PRIVATE_KEY`) are already configured on the repository.

## Design notes

* **Preflight keys on the App ID, not the private key** — an ID is not itself a credential. The mint step needs both, so a *half*-configured App fails there rather than skipping. That split is intended: "not set up yet" skips, "set up wrong" reds.
* **One mint per run is enough** — the token lives an hour and the job is `timeout-minutes: 20`. The action masks the token in logs and revokes it in its post-step, so it does not outlive the run.
* Token scoped to this repository by default (the action defaults `repositories` to the current repo), carrying only `contents:write` (the stamping push) and `pull-requests:write` (release-plz opening/updating the PR).

## Acceptance criteria

1. No `secrets.RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN` reference remains in `.github/`.
2. `repo:actionlint` passes.
3. With the App secrets absent the job still skips cleanly green; with them present it mints and proceeds.
4. AC3's second half is only observable once this is on `main` — the first push produces a real `release-pr` run.

## Expected first observation

release-plz's baseline is the crates.io registry, not git tags, and `rs/release-plz.toml` sets no `git_only`. At the `0.1.0` floor the expected behaviour is an **empty release PR** (manifest version proposed, no bump) — not evidence of a broken token.

## Follow-up left open

`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-22-sma-576-kernel-floor-and-lockstep-gate.md:1120` still describes the `RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN` shape. Deliberately not touched — it is a dated record of what SMA-576 planned, not live guidance. Unblocks the corresponding checklist item in SMA-580.

input.command:
cd /Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-core
gh pr create --base main --title "ci(release): mint the app installation token in-workflow (SMA-589)" --body-file - <<'BODY'
## Why

SMA-580's checklist requires the release token to be "issued from the **existing Paigasus bot GitHub App**". As shipped, `release.yml` could not consume such a token.

The `release-pr` job (SMA-576) read `RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN` as a **static** secret in two places:

- `release.yml:109` — `GIT_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN }}`
- `release.yml:133` — interpolated into `REDACTED`

A GitHub App **installation token expires after one hour**, so it cannot live in a repository secret. Minting one needs an `actions/create-github-app-token` step, and there was none — `secrets.RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN` was the only secret referenced anywhere under `.github/`.

So the shipped shape could only ever have held a long-lived PAT. That sits badly against the surrounding posture (pinned action SHAs, `persist-credentials: false` / artipacked hardening, osv-scanner, cargo-deny) — and against the design's own intent: the `x-access-token:` username and the hardcoded `paigasus-release[bot]` committer at lines 154-155 are both App-shaped. The minting step was simply never added, presumably because the job shipped inert.

**Why it stayed invisible:** the preflight makes the job skip cleanly green while the secret is absent. That is deliberate and correct — an unguarded job would have reddened `main` on every push — but it means nothing in CI ever exercised the token path.

## What changed

Four sites, all in `.github/workflows/release.yml`:

1. Preflight now keys on `secrets.PAIGASUS_BOT_APP_ID` instead of `RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN`; same skip-clean-green behaviour and the same reason it cannot be a job-level `if:`.
2. New `app_token` step — `actions/create-github-app-token` pinned to `bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1` (v3.2.0), guarded by the preflight, placed before Checkout.
3. `GIT_TOKEN` and `GH_TOKEN_FOR_PUSH` now read `steps.app_token.outputs.token`.
4. Header comment updated to stop naming the removed secret.

## Design notes

- **The preflight keys on the App ID, not the private key** — an ID is not itself a credential, so it stays diagnosable. The mint step requires both, so a *half*-configured App fails there rather than skipping. That split is intended: "not set up yet" skips, "set up wrong" reds.
- **One mint per run suffices** — the token lives an hour against `timeout-minutes: 20`. The action masks it in logs and revokes it in its post-step, so it does not outlive the run.
- Token is scoped to this repository by default, carrying only `contents:write` (the stamping push) and `pull-requests:write` (release-plz opening/updating the PR).
- The existing `persist-credentials: false` comment is untouched — its reasoning holds unchanged, and arguably improves, since the token now self-revokes.

## Verification

- `moon run repo:actionlint` — passes.
- YAML parses with steps in the intended order: `preflight` → `app_token` → `Checkout` → …
- No `secrets.RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN` reference remains under `.github/`.
- Both secrets confirmed present on the repository (`PAIGASUS_BOT_APP_ID`, `PAIGASUS_BOT_PRIVATE_KEY`).

The live half — the job actually minting and proceeding — is only observable once this is on `main`, since the workflow triggers on push to `main`.

## Expected first observation after merge

release-plz's baseline is the crates.io registry rather than git tags, and `rs/release-plz.toml` sets no `git_only`. At the `0.1.0` floor the expected result is an **empty release PR** (manifest version proposed, no bump) — that is success, not a broken token.

## Left deliberately

`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-22-sma-576-kernel-floor-and-lockstep-gate.md:1120` still describes the `RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN` shape. It is a dated record of what SMA-576 planned, not live guidance.

content.text:
Checks were green, but I didn't merge — two things came up that you should know about:

**1. CodeRabbit found a real issue, and it contradicted something I wrote.**

zizmor's `github-app` rule flagged: *"app token inherits blanket installation permissions."* My comment claimed the token carried "only what the App is granted" — describing the inherited set as if it were a guarantee. It isn't. Without `permission-*` inputs the token inherits **every** permission the installation holds, so granting the App an unrelated scope later would silently widen this token. Fixed in `d50c105`:

```yaml
permission-contents: write
permission-pull-requests: write
```

Comment corrected to match. Note the action *errors* if asked for a permission the App doesn't hold — which is the right direction, and consistent with the preflight design: an under-granted App reds at mint time rather than half-working later. If the App wasn't granted both, this is where you'll find out.

I replied on the thread and resolved it.

**2. PR 168 (SMA-572/573) merged while we waited**, so #169 was `BEHIND`. Rebased onto `3eed2b6` and force-pushed with `--force-with-lease`.

Current branch state:
```
d50c105 ci(release): request the app token's two permissions explicitly
9df02ae ci(release): mint the app installation token in-workflow (SMA-589)
3eed2b6 (origin/main) ci(ci): script-pin the remaining self-scheduled gates … (SMA-572)
```

`repo:actionlint` passes locally on the amended file. A fresh check run is in flight on the new head — I'm watching it and will merge once it's green.

One thing worth flagging now rather than after the merge: because the permissions are explicit, the very first real `release-pr` run doubles as a check on the App's grants. If it errors at the mint step, that's the App missing `contents:write` or `pull-requests:write` — not this workflow.
